title: Narrow string storage cleanup
summary: Recovered 0x415b60 as a 24-byte string member cleanup: unsigned capacity >=16 invokes the scalar-delete binding on the first pointer, then resets capacity to 15, length to zero, and storage byte zero. Other storage bytes survive. Callers pass ECX pointing at stack locals; no arguments or meaningful return value. The embedding port supplies riff::scalar_delete.
test_description: 396 direct original-versus-C++ cases over capacities 0,1,14,15,16,17,31,255,0x7fffffff,0x80000000,0xffffffff; six lengths including inconsistent/extreme values; null and live-buffer heap pointers; three byte patterns. Checks full object and surrounding guards, untouched storage bytes, delete argument/count, pre-reset callback observations, callback buffer side effects, and repeated cleanup without release. Audited cdecl callback mapped via .delete_iat at 0x92d4b0.
known_limits: Requires 32-bit pointer layout, matching the original ABI; a 64-bit port needs an explicit layout adaptation.
Delete is an injected platform binding; controlled callbacks do not validate CRT allocation/deallocation internals.
Windows FS/SEH and exception-unwind behavior are not tested. On a throwing delete the source performs no subsequent reset; this path is not exercised.
No matching-byte claim; pinned native MSVC validation is performed separately by the coordinator.
